# Setups of the two studies {#sec-app-setup}

## Simulation design

The data follow the model in @eq-model with $i = 1, \dots, G$ curves. Responses are generated on a
grid of 241 points in $t \in [0, 1]$ and subsampled to $D = 61$ (default) or 241 points; the
functional covariate is observed on 51 points in $s \in [0, 1]$:
$X_i(s) = \xi_{i0} + \sum_{k=1}^{29} \xi_{ik}\sqrt 2 \cos(k\pi s)$ with independent
$\xi_{ik} \sim N(0, (k+1)^{-2})$. Its centered spectrum (first principal component 62% of the
variance, four components 88%, rank 24 at 99.5%) matches the corpus-callosum profiles of the
baseline DTI data in refund (67%, 86%, 26). The low-rank variant uses variances $(k+1)^{-3}$ (rank 9).
The scalar covariate is $v_i \sim N(0, 1)$. The smooth-effect model replaces the functional term by
$f(x_i, t)$ with $x_i \sim U(0, 1)$.

Truths are fixed functions projected by least squares onto the fitted bases, so they are exactly
representable: $\beta(s,t) = \cos(\pi s)\sin(\pi t) + (s - 1/2)\cos(2\pi t)$,
$f(x,t) = 2(x - 1/2)\cos(\pi t) + t\sin(\pi x)$, $\gamma(t) = \sin(2\pi t)$. The rough truth adds
$0.6\sin(3\pi s)\sin(3\pi t)$ to $\beta$ and $f$ and $0.5\sin(5\pi t)$ to $\gamma$. Truths are scaled
so that the non-intercept signal $S = \int \mathrm{Var}_{X,z}\{\eta(t) - \alpha(t)\}\,dt$ is 1 (80% from
the main term, 20% from $\gamma$) and multiplied by $\sqrt S$ per family. The intercept is a Gaussian
bump plus a constant that sets the average response level (mean count 3, prevalence 0.2).

The fitted bases are cubic B-splines with first-order difference penalties [@Eilers1996; @Wood2017] (mgcv's `ps` basis with `m = c(2, 1)`), so constants along each direction are unpenalized; $k = 12$ along $t$ for the
intercept and $\gamma$; an $8 \times 10$ tensor product for $\beta$; $8 \times 12$ for $f$. The larger
bases halve and quarter the knot spacing (about 100, 260 and 790 coefficients).

Within-curve errors
are a zero-mean process with correlation kernel $R$, scaled for Gaussian responses and used as the
latent layer of a Gaussian copula for the other families, $Y_{ij} = F^{-1}_{ij}\{\Phi(Z_{ij})\}$, so
each marginal is exactly the fitted family and the working model is wrong only about the dependence.
The kernels are: independent; rough stationary $0.8\exp(-|t-t'|/0.089) + 0.2\,\mathbb 1\{t=t'\}$; smooth: the
residual covariance of a REML fit to the DTI data (24 eigenfunctions plus 6% white noise, as a
correlation kernel); exact AR(1) $\exp(-|t-t'|/0.071)$; sign-changing
$0.8\exp(-|t-t'|/0.3)\cos(2\pi|t-t'|/0.4) + 0.2\,\mathbb 1\{t=t'\}$; heteroskedastic versions of the
smooth kernel with the DTI variance profile along $t$, a subject scale $\exp(0.5 v_i - 0.25)$, or both. @fig-kernels shows the homoskedastic kernels.

```{r}
#| label: fig-kernels
#| fig-cap: "Error processes of the simulation: correlation kernels $R(t,t')$ (top) and two sample curves of the latent Gaussian process (bottom, same draws of standard normals across processes), on the default grid of $D = 61$ points. The main factorial uses the first three."
#| fig-height: 3
fig_kernels()
```

Under misregistration, $Y_i(t_j) = \eta_i(h_i(t_j)) + \varepsilon_i(h_i(t_j))$ with
$h_i(t) = t + a_i\sin(\pi t)/\pi$, $a_i \sim N(0, 0.314^2)$ truncated at $|a_i| \le 0.9$, and
errors are independent. Gaussian misregistration settings score the warp-averaged coefficient functions, GLM settings
only the exact observed-clock mean.

The signal is $R^2 \in \{0.2, 0.5, 0.8\}$ for Gaussian responses and $\sqrt S \in \{0.5, 1\}$ on the link scale
for Poisson and binary responses. The extended families are run at the default signal: scaled $t$ (4 df) as
Gaussian at $R^2 = 0.5$; beta ($\phi = 20$, mean 0.3) and negative binomial (size 5, mean 3) at
$\sqrt S = 0.5$.

The 20-curve block uses the first 20 curves of each replicate of the main factorial,
so it shares its draws with the 40- and 100-curve settings. The zero-surface block sets
$\beta \equiv 0$ in the smooth-truth setting at the default signal, for Gaussian and binary responses
with independent and smooth errors and 40 and 100 curves; $\gamma$, the intercept bump and the
Gaussian error variance are those of the non-zero setting, and the intercept constant of binary
responses is reset to keep the prevalence at 0.2.

All random draws depend only on the replicate index, so contrasts between settings
and intervals are paired. Each setting has `r unique(S$n_rep)` replicates; none failed. Concurvity of
the fitted terms (mgcv's worst case) is at most `r f(max(CONC$concurvity), 2)`. The next table lists the
blocks of settings: the main factorial (family × error process × $G$ × signal) and extensions that
each change one factor.

```{r s2-design}
#| output: asis
stab(blocks |> select(block, cells, families, errors, G, signal, truth, D, model, covariate, basis) |>
  mutate(block = gsub("_", " ", recode(block, core = "main factorial", small_G = "main factorial, G = 20", null_beta = "zero surface", warp = "misregistration", ar1_home = "exact AR(1)", warp_ar1 = "misreg. (AR(1) fit)", families = "extended families", term_type = "smooth effect", oscillating = "sign-changing", lowrank_covariate = "low-rank covariate", basis_size = "larger bases")),
    model = recode(model, `ff(X)` = "functional", `f(x,t)` = "smooth effect"), truth = recode(truth, null = "zero"), covariate = recode(covariate, lowrank = "low-rank")) |> rename(settings = cells),
  "Blocks of the simulation design. Error processes: indep. independent, rough rough stationary, smooth from the DTI residuals, AR(1) exact AR(1), sign-chg. sign-changing, var(t)/var(z)/var(t,z) heteroskedastic versions of smooth, misreg. misregistration. Truth: smooth, rough or zero. Signal: low, default, high. Bases: default, 2× or 4× finer knots.", font = 7, landscape = TRUE)
```

Each replicate is fitted by REML and curve-blocked NCV (mgcv `gam`); by pointwise (non-blocked) NCV in the
Gaussian settings at $G = 100$ with independent, smooth and sign-changing errors; and by the AR(1) working
model in the Gaussian settings at $G = 100$ with dependent errors. The AR(1) model is fitted with
mgcv's `bam()` by fast REML with AR(1) errors that restart at the first grid point of each curve.
Its correlation $\rho$ is profiled over the grid $\{0, 0.1, \dots, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99\}$ by the fast-REML
criterion, which includes the log-determinant of the whitening transform; the best grid value is
then refined by a one-dimensional search between its two neighboring grid values. Its intervals are
model-based from that fit. The plasmode study uses the same fit.

Some NCV fits were flagged as not converged, meaning that mgcv's search over the smoothing parameters ended without
meeting its convergence test:
`r f(100 * cflag_rate("fpc"), 0)`% of scaled-$t$ fits under smooth errors and `r f(100 * cflag_rate("iid"), 0)`%
under independent errors, `r f(100 * (1 - conv_ncv$conv[conv_ncv$fit_family == "betar"]), 1)`% of beta fits, and
fewer than 0.1% otherwise (settings with at least 40 curves and a non-zero surface; at most
`r f(100 * pm_flag_max, 1)`% per combination in the plasmode study). No REML fit in these settings was flagged, so
the study says nothing about intervals from non-converged REML fits.

We refitted flagged scaled-$t$ fits from the REML smoothing parameters and from ten times those values. For the first five flagged fits, all with independent errors, the refits reach the same criterion within
`r sci_tex(max(tapply(SCAT$criterion, SCAT$task, \(x) diff(range(x)))))` and the same surface within
`r sci_tex(max(SCAT$beta_max_diff))`. Of `r nrow(scat_spread)` randomly chosen flagged fits with smooth errors,
`r nrow(scat_same)` reach the same criterion within `r f(max(scat_same$crit), 3)`, the same surface within
`r f(max(scat_same$surf), 3)` and the same CL2 standard errors within `r f(100 * max(scat_same$se), 1)`%, consistent with
a flat optimum; in an 18th the study fit's criterion is `r f(scat_near$study_above, 1)` above the refits', with the surface
within `r f(scat_near$surf, 2)`. In the other two, a refit returns a materially different fit, its surface moved by about
twice the root-mean-square size of the true surface (`r f(scat_truth_rms, 1)`). In one, the study fit has the worse
criterion, by `r f(scat_study_worse$study_above, 0)`, and the standard errors differ by up to
`r f(100 * scat_study_worse$se, 0)`%; in the other, a refit is worse by `r f(scat_refit_worse$worst_refit_above, 0)`, with standard errors
up to `r f(100 * scat_refit_worse$se, 0)`% larger. `r scat_refit_flagged$f` of the `r scat_refit_flagged$n` refits were flagged too. A
flag thus does not separate these fits from the stable ones.

Under smooth errors, in the `r cflag("ncv_cl2", TRUE, col = "n_rep")` replicates with a flagged NCV fit, the NCV estimate of $\beta$ has median
relative error `r f(cflag("ncv_cl2", TRUE, col = "rel"), 2)` and NCV + CL2 covers `r f(cflag("ncv_cl2", TRUE), 3)`
(Monte Carlo SE `r f(cflag("ncv_cl2", TRUE, col = "coverage_se"), 3)`), against
`r f(cflag("ncv_cl2", FALSE, col = "rel"), 2)` and `r f(cflag("ncv_cl2", FALSE), 3)` (`r f(cflag("ncv_cl2", FALSE, col = "coverage_se"), 3)`)
in the `r cflag("ncv_cl2", FALSE, col = "n_rep")` other replicates; this difference of `r pp(max(abs(cflag_gap$gap)))` is the largest coverage
gap of NCV + CL2 over estimands and error processes. The model-based NCV intervals cover
`r f(cflag("ncv_model", TRUE), 3)` and `r f(cflag("ncv_model", FALSE), 3)`, REML + CL2 `r f(cflag("reml_cl2", TRUE), 3)`
and `r f(cflag("reml_cl2", FALSE), 3)` in the same two groups, so part of the gap may reflect harder data. The flag is not randomly
assigned and the comparison is descriptive.

Low-smoothing NCV fits (@sec-res-estimation) were examined in the main factorial and in the settings with denser
grids, other families, rough truths, AR(1) errors and misregistration (`r lowsm("n_cells", "independent") + lowsm("n_cells") + sum(LOWSM_WARP$n_cells)` settings with 40 or 100 curves), with the tail defined on the first surface penalty.
Under dependence, apart from misregistration, cutoffs of $e^4$ and $e^2$ give `r f(100 * lowsm("share_low", thr = 4), 0)`% and `r f(100 * lowsm("share_low", thr = 2), 0)`% of NCV fits, and applying the $e^3 \approx 20$ cutoff to either penalty
gives `r f(100 * lowsm("share_low_either"), 1)`%. Under misregistration, NCV's smoothing parameters are the more variable
ones, with up to `r f(100 * max(LOWSM_WARP$share_low), 0)`% of fits below the $e^3$ cutoff (Poisson).
Under dependence, apart from misregistration, the share of low-smoothing fits is `r rng(100 * LOWSM_DEP$share_low, 1)`% across families and
error processes, and these fits have `r f(lowsm("within_edf_low"), 1)` times their setting's median surface EDF, still fewer than REML's on all of them.
REML also does worse on these replicates: its error is `r f(lowsm("within_reml_low"), 1)` times its median and its CL2 intervals cover
`r f(lowsm("cov_reml_low"), 3)` (NCV + CL2: `r f(lowsm("cov_ncv_low"), 3)`). On the remaining replicates, REML's mean squared error is
`r f(lowsm("mse_ratio_other"), 1)` rather than `r f(lowsm("mse_ratio_all"), 1)` times NCV's (geometric means over settings). The converse does not hold: on the
`r f(100 * lowsm("share_low_reml"), 0)`% of replicates in REML's own lower tail, NCV's error stays near its median (`r f(lowsm("within_ncv_remltail"), 2)` times) and its coverage is
`r pp(-lowsm("cov_diff_ncv_remltail"))` lower than on the other replicates.

## Plasmode datasets

A plasmode simulation [@FranklinSchneeweissPolinskiRassen2014] keeps the real covariates and real
error structure of a dataset and replaces only the true regression function by a known one.

```{r s3-datasets}
#| output: asis
ds_text <- DS |> mutate(
  source = if_else(app == "ecg_gls4b", "myocardial-strain study, first beat per subject", source),
  source = if_else(app == "af", "atrial-fibrillation trial, patients randomized to digoxin or a beta-blocker", source),
  access = if_else(startsWith(access, "local"), "non-public; aggregates only", access),
  source = sub(" via tidyfundata::running", "", source, fixed = TRUE),
  covariate = sub(" (presumed from the documented lead order)", "", covariate, fixed = TRUE),
  prep = sub("; lead identities resolved from the R-wave progression", "", prep, fixed = TRUE),
  grid_note = sub(" (as in the original 16 cells)", "", grid_note, fixed = TRUE)
) |> mutate(across(where(is.character), \(x) {
  x <- gsub("isation", "ization", x, fixed = TRUE)
  gsub("(normal|digit|standard|random)ised", "\\1ized", x)
}))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ds_text))) {
  d <- ds_text[i, ]
  cat(sprintf(
    "**%s** (%s; %s; %s). %d curves; response: %s, native grid %s (fitted: %s); functional covariate: %s; scalar covariate: %s. Preprocessing: %s. REML fit: $R^2$ %s, surface EDF %s (NCV fit: %s); residual design effect %s, lag-one correlation %s, %s%% negative correlations, %d principal components for 90%% of the residual variance, covariate rank %d.\n\n",
    d$dataset, if (d$role == "counted") "independent curves" else "dependent curves", d$source, d$access, d$G,
    d$response, d$native, d$grid_note, d$covariate, d$z, d$prep,
    f(d$R2, 2), f(d$edf_ff_REML, 1), f(d$edf_ff_NCV, 1), f(d$DE, 1), f(d$lag1, 2), f(100 * d$neg_share, 0),
    as.integer(d$fpc90), as.integer(d$rank_X)
  ))
}
```

The ECG strain beats were recorded with 29 to 83 frames and interpolated to 61 grid points;
interpolation adds smoothness within a curve, so part of the residual dependence of that dataset,
and of its design effect, comes from the interpolation.

Six datasets have independent source curves. The other three have serially
(ocean, electricity) or spatially (weather) dependent source curves.

The residual *design effect* of a dataset
is $\mathbf 1^\top\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf 1/\operatorname{tr}\boldsymbol\Sigma$ for the covariance
$\boldsymbol\Sigma$ of its REML residual curves: the factor by which the variance of a grid mean
exceeds its working-independence value.

```{r t-s3-models-1}
#| output: asis
stab(model_tab |> select(-model), "Fitted models: bases (intercept, $\\gamma$; surface $8 \\times 10$), $R^2$ of the REML fit, surface and total EDF of the three fits used as truths (REML / NCV / midpoint), and whether the midpoint fit lies between the two for every term.", font = 6)
```

```{r t-s3-models-3}
#| output: asis
stab(dep_tab |> select(-role), "Residual dependence and covariate diagnostics (REML residual curves): design effect DE and DE$/D$, residual correlation at one grid step and at 10% and 25% of the domain, share of negative correlations and the most negative one, max/min SD along $t$, principal components for 90% of the residual variance, centered covariate rank, share of response variance removed by registration.", font = 6, landscape = TRUE)
```

```{r t-s3-models-4}
#| output: asis
stab(block_tab, "Datasets with dependent source curves: block construction for the block flips and block-wise NCV; residual-score correlation within and between blocks.", font = 6)
```

## Construction of the plasmode data

Each dataset's model, $Y_i(t) = \alpha(t) + \int X_i(s)\beta(s,t)\,ds + v_i\gamma(t) + \varepsilon_i(t)$
(Gaussian), is fitted by REML and by curve-blocked NCV. The fitted means of three fits serve as
truths: the REML fit (*REML-fitted truth*), the NCV fit (*NCV-fitted truth*) and a refit with every
smoothing parameter at the geometric mean of the two fits' values (*midpoint truth*). Replicate data
are these fitted means plus each subject's own residual curve from the REML or the NCV fit, multiplied by an
independent random sign per curve. Sign flipping keeps each residual curve's within-curve covariance
and makes the curves independent across subjects. For the ECG strain data, heartbeat difference
curves $(Y_{i1} - Y_{i2})/\sqrt 2$ of two beats per subject are a further error source, not shaped by any fit, used on their own scale or rescaled to the
average variance of the REML residuals.

Each
combination of dataset, truth and residual source is run with all subjects and with 40 randomly
chosen subjects (`r unique(P$n_rep)` replicates each). The three datasets with dependent source curves add block flips
(one sign per block of neighboring curves) and block-wise NCV and CL2. The mean is evaluated at the
covariates of a fixed set of 50 subjects of the dataset, at the native grid points. There are
`r nrow(P |> distinct(app, truth, residual, flip, error, G))` combinations in all.

```{r t-s3-cohort}
#| output: asis
stab(cohort, "Choice of the fixed set of 50 subjects for the mean: the rule used, and the balance check of the first 50 subjects against the remaining subjects (one-sided test at 5%, permutation p-value, standardized mean differences of the scalar covariate and the first three covariate scores). Where this check failed, a seeded random sample of 50 subjects was used; the balance of that sample was not recorded.", font = 6)
```
